options.C: Hardly the tourist does speaks English.

questions.stem: Describe an occasion in your life when you were very happy or very sad.
questions.answer: One of the saddest moments in my life was the day my grandfather passed away. He was not just a relative but my mentor and best friend. I remember the gloomy Tuesday morning when the phone rang, and the silence that followed my father's conversation told me everything. The house, usually filled with his laughter and the smell of his favorite coffee, suddenly felt cold and empty. During the funeral, seeing his peaceful face made the reality sink in—I would never hear his stories about the old days again. For weeks, I felt a profound void in my heart. However, as time passed, I began to realize that he lived on through the values he taught me. This experience taught me the fragility of life and the importance of cherishing every moment with loved ones. Although the pain of his absence remains, the memories of his wisdom and kindness continue to guide me, turning my grief into a source of strength and inspiration.

questions.stem: Write a paragraph supporting or opposing the argument that 'News from mass media is important in everybody's life'.
questions.answer: In the contemporary world, news from mass media plays an indispensable role in our daily lives. I strongly support the argument that it is vital for everyone. Firstly, mass media serves as a primary source of information, keeping us updated on global events, political shifts, and scientific breakthroughs. Without it, we would be isolated in our local bubbles, unaware of the challenges and triumphs of the wider world. Secondly, it acts as a tool for education and awareness. Through documentaries and investigative journalism, people learn about social issues, health crises, and environmental changes, which empowers them to make informed decisions. Furthermore, mass media provides a platform for diverse voices, fostering a sense of global community and shared humanity. While critics point to the dangers of misinformation, the solution lies in media literacy rather than dismissal. In conclusion, mass media is the window through which we view the world; it broadens our horizons and ensures we remain active, informed citizens in an increasingly interconnected society.

questions.stem: Write a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph of about 200 words on the following topic: **Describe an occasion in your life when you were very happy or very sad.**
questions.answer: One of the saddest occasions in my life was the day my grandfather passed away. It was a rainy Tuesday afternoon when we received the news. He had been a pillar of strength for our family, always ready with a wise story or a warm smile. The house, which used to be filled with his booming laughter and the scent of his old pipe, suddenly felt cold and empty. Seeing my father, usually a stoic man, break down in tears was heartbreaking. We gathered in the living room, sharing memories of his kindness and the lessons he taught us about perseverance. Although the grief was overwhelming, that day also taught me the importance of family bonds. We supported each other through the funeral arrangements and the long days of mourning. Even though he is gone, the values he instilled in us remain. This experience was profoundly sad because it marked the end of an era for our family, but it also made me cherish the time I spend with my loved ones even more, realizing how fragile life can be.

questions.stem: Write a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph of about 200 words on the following topic: **Write a paragraph supporting or opposing the argument that 'News from mass media is important in everybody's life'.**
questions.answer: In the modern era, news from mass media has become an indispensable part of daily life. I strongly support the argument that mass media is vital because it serves as the primary source of information and education for the global population. Firstly, mass media keeps us informed about significant world events, from political shifts to environmental crises, allowing citizens to make informed decisions. For instance, during health emergencies, the media provides crucial safety guidelines that can save lives. Furthermore, it acts as a bridge between different cultures, fostering a sense of global community by sharing stories from far-off places. However, the importance of media also brings the responsibility of critical thinking. With the rise of 'fake news,' individuals must learn to verify sources. Despite this challenge, the role of media in promoting transparency and holding authorities accountable cannot be understated. Without mass media, people would live in isolation, unaware of the forces shaping their world. Therefore, it is not just a tool for entertainment, but a fundamental pillar of a functioning democracy and an informed society.
